configuration.summary:
I see skills not just as items on a list, but as abilities developed through curiosity, practice, experience, and continuous learning. Some have grown through building projects, others through academic pursuits, professional responsibilities, or personal exploration.

This page brings together the technologies, tools, and areas of knowledge I've worked with, along with what each of them means to me. Where possible, I've connected a skill to the projects or milestones that helped me develop it. Others stand on their own, representing knowledge and abilities worth sharing in their own right.

More than a measure of proficiency, this is a reflection of what I've explored, what I've learned, and how I've grown along the way.

skills.title: C#
skills.description: My journey with C# began during my academic years, where I developed a strong foundation in programming and object-oriented principles. Through continuous hands-on development, I deepened my understanding of the language, exploring its features and capabilities while building real-world software. Over time, working on complex applications and solving challenging engineering problems turned C# into one of my core programming languages.

skills.title: .NET
skills.description: My experience with .NET grew through building and maintaining real-world applications, progressing from developing backend services to designing scalable application architectures. Working extensively with ASP.NET Core, Entity Framework Core, dependency injection, and the broader .NET ecosystem has given me practical experience in building robust, maintainable, and scalable software solutions.

skills.title: Python
skills.description: My journey with Python has been entirely self-driven, fueled by curiosity and a passion for exploring technology. Through independent learning and hands-on experimentation, I have developed practical programming skills, explored its versatile ecosystem, and used Python to solve problems, automate tasks, and bring ideas to life.
